instructions: Heat the oven to 350°F. Butter a 9-inch square or round baking dish with 1 tbsp of the butter and coat it with 2 tbsp of the breadcrumbs.

Peel the potatoes and cut them into 1 1/2-inch chunks. Put them in a large pot, cover with cold water and add 1 tbsp of salt. Bring to a boil and cook for 15 to 18 minutes, until a fork slides in easily.
Drain the potatoes and return them to the hot pot for 1 minute to dry out. Mash them with a masher or put them through a ricer until smooth.
Let the mash cool for 10 minutes. Hot potatoes would scramble the eggs.
Stir in the eggs, 3 tbsp of the Parmesan, the milk, 1 tsp salt and the pepper until smooth.
Slice the mozzarella thin. Spread half the mash in the dish in an even layer. Cover it with half the ham, all the mozzarella and then the rest of the ham.
Spread the remaining mash over the top in a smooth layer.
Sprinkle the remaining breadcrumbs and 1 tbsp Parmesan over the top and dot with the last 1 tbsp butter, cut into small pieces.
Bake for 35 minutes, until the top is golden and crisp and the edges are bubbling. Let it stand for 5 to 10 minutes so it holds together when you cut it.
Serve in squares. Leftovers keep in the fridge for 3 days; reheat covered in a 350°F oven for 15 minutes. It doesn't freeze well.
method_notes: Your Guardian Chef leads (4.88 from 8 plus 3 unreviewed ratings, so a fallback): mashed potatoes bound with egg and Parmesan, layered around mozzarella and ham, with a breadcrumb crust. Pasta Grammar makes it with butter in the mash instead of milk. The lead's optional béchamel, boiled eggs and mortadella are left out, and the amounts are cut to about 4 servings. The honest time is a little over an hour.
